It fails on empty strings and on missing fields as well as on true nulls, because all three mean the same thing to somebody reading a report. This rule needs no parameters. It is the cheapest check to write and usually the first one worth adding to a new contract, since a column that is sometimes blank will break almost any downstream calculation. When it fails on a large share of rows, the usual cause is an upstream export that changed which columns it includes rather than a genuine data-entry problem, so check the file header before chasing individual records.

query: What does a not null rule check for?
answer: A not-null rule asserts that a column always carries a value.
